source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A 6-year-old has intense itching around the anus at night and disturbed sleep. The best way to confirm pinworm infection is:
questions.rationale: Enterobius eggs are laid on perianal skin; collect by tape swab in the morning before bathing or defecation.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Enterobius vermicularis (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: the choice of diagnosis is recovery of eggs using the Scotch tape method in swabbing the perianal region

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: To prevent spread of pinworm within the family, the nurse teaches:
questions.rationale: Pinworm spreads by ingestion or inhalation of eggs from fingers, linens and objects; hygiene and boiling linens prevent it.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Enterobius vermicularis (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Personal hygiene like proper hand washing and keeping finger nails short must be advocated.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child with heavy roundworm (Ascaris) infection had cough and fever before abdominal symptoms. The cough is due to:
questions.rationale: Ascaris larvae undergo lung migration, causing chest pain, cough and fever before settling in the small intestine.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Ascaris lumbricoides (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Upon ingestion, the larva is released from the eggs and then undergoes lung migration.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which complication can occur when a child harbors a very large number of Ascaris worms?
questions.rationale: Heavy worm burden can cause intestinal obstruction; worms may also migrate to the bile duct or liver.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Ascaris lumbricoides (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: At times patients may harbor a high number ofworms resulting to intestinal obstruction.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A farmer who works barefoot in the fields has pallor and low hemoglobin. The parasite most likely responsible is:
questions.rationale: Hookworm larvae penetrate bare skin; adult worms suck blood from the intestinal wall, causing iron-deficiency anemia.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Hookworms (PDF p. 363)
questions.quote: For as long as the worm is attached, the patient suffers from a constant blood loss which may result to microcytic hypochromic anemia.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: The most specific preventive advice against hookworm infection is to:
questions.rationale: Hookworm enters through skin contact with contaminated soil; footwear and sanitary toilets prevent it.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Hookworms (PDF p. 370)
questions.quote: Health education must be strongly advocated in relation to use of. sanitary toilet facilities and wearing of appropriate footwear like slippers, shoes and/ or boots.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A man develops seizures; CT shows cysts in the brain. He lives where pigs roam near unsanitary toilets. The likely cause is:
questions.rationale: Accidental ingestion of T. solium eggs leads to cysticerci in tissues including the brain (neurocysticercosis), a cause of seizures.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Taenia (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Involvement of the central nervous system is called neurocysticerosis. Many cases of seizures of unknown origin have been associated with this condition.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: To prevent beef and pork tapeworm infection, the nurse advises:
questions.rationale: Man gets adult Taenia infection from raw or undercooked pork or beef containing cysticerci.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Taenia (PDF p. 370)
questions.quote: Health education must emphasize thorough cooking of meat.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A man from Sorsogon who often eats raw freshwater crabs has chronic cough with blood-tinged sputum. Sputum is negative for AFB. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Paragonimus westermani (lung fluke) comes from raw crabs and mimics TB; eggs are found in sputum or stool.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Paragonimus westermani (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: the condition can be misdiagnosed and wrongly treated as pulmonary tuberculosis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Villagers in Ilocos who eat raw freshwater fish develop severe chronic diarrhea, weight loss and edema; some die. The likely parasite is:
questions.rationale: Capillariasis, first described in the Philippines, comes from raw fish and causes intractable diarrhea, malabsorption and death if untreated.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Capillaria philippinensis (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: Man acquires the infection upon ingestion of raw or improperly cooked fish

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A food handler has no symptoms but passes amoeba cysts in his stool. The nurse knows that he:
options: Can spread it as a carrier
questions.rationale: Asymptomatic cyst passers are sources of infection; food handlers need regular stool examination under the Sanitation Code.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Entamoeba histolytica (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: Infected individuals harboring cysts are asymptomatic. However, they are cyst passers and can, therefore, be the extra source of infection in the community.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A watery stool specimen is collected to look for amoeba trophozoites. The nurse should:
options: Send it to the lab immediately
questions.rationale: Trophozoites are fragile and die within 30–60 minutes outside the host, so the specimen must be examined at once.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Entamoeba histolytica (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: trophozoites are fragile and they die within 30 to 60 minutes outside the host.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: When water from a source of doubtful safety must be used for drinking, the best household measure against amoebiasis and giardiasis is:
questions.rationale: Boiling drinking water from questionable sources destroys protozoan cysts.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Entamoeba histolytica (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Boiling of drinking water from questionable source is a very good practice to avoid infection.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Greasy, frothy, foul-smelling stools with bloating and flatus after drinking untreated water suggest:
questions.rationale: Giardia lamblia lives in the small intestine; chronic infection causes greasy, frothy stools and flatus.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Giardia lamblia (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Chronic infection is characterized by passage of greasy, frothy stools.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Malaria is transmitted in the Philippines mainly by the bite of the infected female:
questions.rationale: All human Plasmodia are transmitted by female Anopheles; the major local vector is Anopheles flavirostris.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Plasmodia (PDF p. 379)
questions.quote: All of these species are bansmitted through the bite of the infected female mosquitoes belonging to the GenusAnopheles.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which malaria species is the most dangerous because it can cause cerebral malaria?
questions.rationale: P. falciparum causes severe complications such as cerebral involvement and is the most common species in the Philippines.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Plasmodia (PDF p. 379)
questions.quote: P. falciparum is considered to be the most dangerous because it causes severe complications such as cerebral involvement.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The chills, high fever and sweating of a malaria paroxysm occur when:
questions.rationale: Paroxysms coincide with rupture of mature schizonts in red blood cells.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Plasmodia (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: When the schizonts are mature, the host red cells rupture and the merozoites are released into the circulation. It is at this point when man usually suffers from the malarial paroxysm

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: In malaria microscopy, the thick blood smear is used mainly for:
questions.rationale: The thick smear is for rapid diagnosis; the thin film identifies the species.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Plasmodia (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: The thick blood smear is useful for rapid diagnosis while the thin blood film is used for species idenffcation.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Families in a malaria-endemic barangay should be taught to:
options: Clear vegetation only in the dry season
questions.rationale: Treated bed nets, house screening and protective clothing at night until early morning (biting time) prevent man-vector contact.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Plasmodia (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: To prevent man-vector contact, use of chemically treated bednets and proper screening of houses are advocated.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Clearing overhanging vegetation along streams helps control malaria because it:
questions.rationale: Anopheles flavirostris breeds in shaded, slow-flowing streams; exposure to sunlight and faster flow eliminate breeding sites.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Home environment (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: clearing stream banks of overhanging vegetation and debris to expose them to sunlight and speed up water flow to eliminate breeding sites of Anopheles flavirostris

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Blood for microfilaria examination in suspected filariasis should be collected:
questions.rationale: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae show nocturnal periodicity, so blood is taken at night.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Filariasis diagnosis (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: blood samples must be collected from 8:00 pm to 4:00 am.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: In the Philippines, the main vector of Wuchereria bancrofti breeds in the leaf axils of abaca and banana plants. It is:
questions.rationale: Aedes poecilus is the local vector of bancroftian filariasis.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Filariasis (PDF p. 381)
questions.quote: In the Philippines, however, the parasite is transmitted by Aedes poecilus which breeds pretty well in the axils of the abaca and banana plants.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Elephantiasis and hydrocele in chronic filariasis result from:
questions.rationale: Death of adult worms triggers immune reactions causing lymphatic obstruction, leading to elephantiasis or hydrocele.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Filariasis (PDF p. 381)
questions.quote: When the adult worms die, there will be an immunological reaction resulting in lymphatic obstruction which in turn can lead to elephantiasis or hydrocoele.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Mass drug administration to eliminate lymphatic filariasis in endemic provinces uses:
questions.rationale: DEC combined with albendazole is used for MDA to eliminate lymphatic filariasis.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Filariasis treatment (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: A combination of diethyl carbamazine and albendazole is being utilized for the so called mass drug administration (MDA)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Schistosoma japonicum infects people when:
options: Cercariae in water penetrate the skin
questions.rationale: Cercariae released from Oncomelania snails penetrate the skin of people wading or bathing in infested water.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Schistosoma japonicum (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: The cercaria is the infective stage and it can actively penetrate the human skin.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The circumoval precipitin test (COPT) is requested together with stool examination to help diagnose:
questions.rationale: Schistosomiasis is confirmed by eggs in stool (Kato-Katz) and supported by the COPT serologic test.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Schistosoma japonicum (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: A serological test to detect antibodies called Circumoval Precipitin Test (COPT) is usually requested together with stool examination.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Many deaths from chronic schistosomiasis are caused by:
questions.rationale: Eggs in the liver cause granulomas and portal hypertension, leading to varices, splenomegaly and ascites.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 15 Schistosoma japonicum (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: Many reported cases of death due to schistosomiasis were caused by rupture of esophageal varices.
